traveler: Leonardo di ser Piero da Vinci
title: The Notary's Bastard: Vinci to Amboise, and the Papers Melzi Carried Home
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Anchiano, the birth entered in the family book
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by Antonio da Vinci's own memorandum; the birthplace is not, and English Wikipedia states plainly that it remains uncertain where Leonardo was born, the Anchiano farmhouse being established only with relative certainty
stops.campa: Ser Piero da Vinci is a notary in Florence and the woman is not his wife. The child is born in a farmhouse on the hillside above the town, on a Saturday night three hours into the dark, and old Antonio enters it in the family book the same night in the flat hand a landholder keeps for a lease or a lambing. Illegitimacy shuts the boy out of the notaries' guild that his father and grandfather and great-grandfather belonged to. It leaves him free to be apprenticed to a painter instead. Where exactly the farmhouse stood is still argued over.
stops.quote: A grandson of mine was born April 15, Saturday, three hours into the night.
stops.quote_source: Antonio da Vinci's family memorandum, State Archive of Florence, cited in Martin Kemp, Leonardo (2004)
suggested_refs: The Casa Natale di Leonardo at Anchiano, above Vinci
Antonio da Vinci's memorandum, State Archive of Florence
sources: Antonio da Vinci memorandum, State Archive of Florence

stops.name: Vinci, Santa Croce: baptism with ten godparents
stops.date_confidence: attested; the baptism the day after the birth, by the parish priest Piero di Bartolomeo Cecci, is fixed by the same memorandum
stops.campa: The day after the birth the priest Piero di Bartolomeo Cecci carries him to the font in the parish church, and ten godparents stand for him. Ten is a great many. The father's family is the landholding family of the district and does not intend the child's standing to be in question, whatever his mother's is. Caterina di Meo Lippi appears in the record and then goes out of it; she is described as a peasant woman and almost nothing else about her is known. The boy is entered as Lionardo, son of Ser Piero.
suggested_refs: The parish church of Santa Croce at Vinci and its font
sources: Charles Nicholl, Leonardo da Vinci: Flights of the Mind (2004)

stops.name: Vinci, the catasto return of the grandfather's house
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year by the Florentine catasto of 1457; the month and day are a default
stops.campa: The tax return of 1457 lists the household of Antonio da Vinci and puts the five-year-old in it: not with his mother, not with his father, but in the grandfather's house among the vines and the olive terraces of the Montalbano slope. Ser Piero is in Florence building a practice and a first marriage. The boy grows up inside a working farm's year, water running in the ditches and birds over the Arno flats, and learns to write and reckon at the level a country notary's son gets, which is to say without Latin.
suggested_refs: The Florentine catasto returns of 1457 for the commune of Vinci
sources: Florentine catasto records, cited in standard biographies

stops.name: Florence, the family comes down from the hills
stops.date_confidence: inferred; Wikipedia gives only that the family moved in the mid-1460s, and the specific year 1464 is a conjecture tied to the death of the grandfather Antonio
stops.campa: The family comes down out of the hills to the city where Ser Piero has his practice. Florence in these years is a town of forty thousand with Donatello lately dead, Verrocchio's furnaces going, and the Medici bank running the credit of half of Europe. The boy arrives into it at twelve or thirteen or fourteen, depending on which biographer is counting, with a country hand and no Latin, and stays in one way or another for the next twenty years. What he does in the first year or two of it, nobody recorded.
suggested_refs: Ser Piero da Vinci's notarial practice in Florence

stops.name: Florence, Verrocchio's shop: the studio boy and the guild
stops.date_confidence: traditional for the entry at about age fourteen, following Vasari; the 1472 guild matriculation is attested. The pin is approximate: the exact address of Verrocchio's bottega is not securely documented
stops.campa: Andrea del Verrocchio is a goldsmith, a bronze caster, a sculptor and a painter, and his shop takes work of every kind: tomb slabs, armour, festival machinery, altarpieces, the copper ball for the cathedral lantern. Leonardo comes in at about fourteen to sweep and grind colours and stays roughly seven years, learning casting and mechanics alongside drawing. In 1472 the Compagnia di San Luca enters him as a qualified master painter, twenty years old and entitled to his own shop. He does not take one. He stays where he is.
suggested_refs: The matriculation register of the Compagnia di San Luca, Florence, 1472
sources: Compagnia di San Luca matriculation records

stops.name: Vinci, the Arno valley drawn and dated
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day: Leonardo inscribed the sheet himself. The vantage point is not fixed by the inscription and the pin follows the traditional identification of the view with the valley below Vinci
stops.campa: He sets down a pen-and-ink view of the valley, the river plain hazing away under a hatched sky, rocks and a fortress worked up on the left, and writes the date on it in his own reversed hand: the fifth of August 1473. No figure appears anywhere in it. It is the earliest sheet by him that carries a date, and it is a landscape for its own sake at a moment when landscape in Italian painting is what happens behind the Virgin's shoulder. He is twenty-one and has been a master painter for a year.
suggested_refs: The dated Arno landscape drawing, Gabinetto dei Disegni e delle Stampe, Uffizi
sources: Uffizi drawing inscribed by Leonardo, 5 August 1473

stops.name: Florence, the angel in the Baptism of Christ
stops.date_confidence: the panel is dated c. 1475 on style; the Vasari anecdote attached to it is legendary and is flagged as such here, the geography and chronology lenses of the research pool disagreeing over whether to tag it attested
stops.campa: Verrocchio's shop delivers a Baptism of Christ, and one of the two kneeling angels at the left is painted in oil, softer and more turned than anything else on the panel. The angel is Leonardo's. Vasari, writing eighty years later, says Verrocchio looked at it, understood that a boy had beaten him, and never picked up a brush again. Nothing outside Vasari attests the renunciation, and Verrocchio went on running the largest sculpture practice in Florence until he died in Venice.
suggested_refs: The Baptism of Christ, Verrocchio and workshop, Uffizi
sources: Vasari, Lives of the Artists, flagged as legendary by modern scholarship

stops.name: Florence, Palazzo del Podestà: the note in the drum
stops.date_confidence: attested to April 1476 by the judicial record; the day of the first denunciation is not carried in the reachable sources and is defaulted
stops.campa: An anonymous note goes into the tamburo, the drum box set out for denunciations, naming four young men and the seventeen-year-old goldsmith's apprentice Jacopo Saltarelli. Leonardo is one of the four. The Ufficiali di Notte take the case up twice and drop it twice for want of witnesses; one of the accused is a Tornabuoni, kin to the Medici by marriage. Nothing follows. The paper stays in the file, which is why the episode is known at all, and Leonardo never mentions it anywhere in the surviving pages.
suggested_refs: Atti degli Ufficiali di Notte, Florentine judicial archive, 1476
sources: Florentine judicial archive, Atti degli Ufficiali di Notte, 1476

stops.name: Florence, San Donato a Scopeto: the Adoration left in wash
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1481 by the commission, though the contract survives only through later scholars' citations of an archive now lost, which is why the research pool tags this stop as reconstruction
stops.campa: The Augustinians outside the walls want an altarpiece and get, instead of a finished panel, the most ambitious composition anyone in Florence has attempted: a ruin in perspective behind, horses fighting in the middle distance, a crowd folded around the Virgin in brown wash and underdrawing. He works it up and leaves it standing. The monks eventually hand the commission to Filippino Lippi. The panel goes unfinished to the Medici and from them, centuries on, to the Uffizi. The contract itself is gone.
suggested_refs: The Adoration of the Magi, unfinished, Uffizi
sources: San Donato a Scopeto commission contract, cited by later scholars

stops.name: Milan, the Corte Vecchia: an engineer offers himself
stops.date_confidence: attested to about 1482 by consensus; the draft letter in the Codex Atlanticus is undated, and the month of arrival is not recorded
stops.campa: He goes north to Ludovico Sforza, and the letter he brings or drafts lists what he can do in ten numbered items. Nine are military: portable bridges, ways to drain a moat, covered chariots, mortars that throw small stones like a tempest, methods of mining under a river. The tenth mentions that he can also work in marble, bronze and clay, and paint as well as any man alive. He is thirty and has finished almost nothing. Milan gives him a studio in the old ducal palace beside the cathedral and keeps him seventeen years.
stops.quote: Most illustrious Lord, Having now sufficiently considered the specimens of all those who proclaim themselves skilled contrivers of instruments of war...
stops.quote_source: Leonardo's letter to Ludovico Sforza, c. 1482, item 1340 in The Notebooks of Leonardo Da Vinci, trans. Jean Paul Richter (1883)
suggested_refs: The draft letter to Ludovico Sforza, Codex Atlanticus, Biblioteca Ambrosiana
sources: Codex Atlanticus, draft letter to Ludovico Sforza

stops.name: Milan, San Francesco Grande: the Virgin of the Rocks and the quarrel
stops.date_confidence: attested to 25 April 1483 by the confraternity contract. The pin approximates the site of San Francesco Grande, demolished in 1806 and built over
stops.campa: The Confraternity of the Immaculate Conception contracts for a panel of the Virgin in a rocky place, with a delivery date and a price. Leonardo paints a grotto lit from behind, four figures on a wet floor of stone, and the confraternity refuses the valuation. The argument runs on for a quarter of a century through petitions to the duke and to the king of France, and ends with two versions of the picture existing, one now in Paris and one in London. The church itself was pulled down in 1806 and its ground built over.
suggested_refs: The confraternity contract and the later petitions, Milan archives
sources: Confraternity of the Immaculate Conception contract and legal petitions, Milan archives

stops.name: Milan, the mirror hand and the first cadavers
stops.date_confidence: attested to about 1489 for the start of systematic anatomical work, on the dating of the Windsor sheets; no single day begins it
stops.campa: He begins cutting. The sheets fill with skulls sectioned along the sagittal line, the layers of the scalp drawn as the rind of an onion, muscles lifted one from another, and the writing runs right to left across the page so that it reads only in a glass. He is left-handed; the mirror hand costs him nothing, and most scholars take it for convenience rather than concealment. He sets down what the work is like, for anyone thinking of taking it up. He works at night, alone, with bodies that will not keep.
stops.quote: And if you should have a love for such things you might be prevented by loathing, and if that did not prevent you, you might be deterred by the fear of living in the night hours in the company of those corpses, quartered and flayed and horrible to see.
stops.quote_source: Anatomical notes, item 796, The Notebooks of Leonardo Da Vinci, trans. Jean Paul Richter (1883)
suggested_refs: The Windsor anatomical sheets, Royal Collection
sources: Leonardo's anatomical notebooks, Royal Collection, Windsor

stops.name: Pavia, the cathedral tower and the antique rider
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1490 by the cathedral fabric payment records, which name both Leonardo and Francesco di Giorgio Martini; the month is not fixed
stops.campa: He rides to Pavia with Francesco di Giorgio Martini, both of them paid to advise on the crossing tower of the cathedral, and while he is there he goes to look at the Regisole, the antique bronze rider standing near the west front. The horse is in motion, one foreleg lifted, and he draws it. His own colossus is waiting in the studio in Milan and will not stand still on paper. The Regisole was smashed by a crowd in 1796; what survives of it is a copy, and Leonardo's notes on how a horse carries its weight.
suggested_refs: The lost Regisole of Pavia and Leonardo's horse studies

stops.name: Milan, Piazza del Castello: the clay colossus
stops.date_confidence: attested to the wedding festivities of Bianca Maria Sforza, November 1493, by Milanese chronicles; the day is not recorded
stops.campa: For the wedding of Bianca Maria Sforza the model comes out under the arch of the castle: a horse in clay, over seven metres from hoof to crest, with no rider yet, meant to be cast in bronze around Francesco Sforza. Milan has never seen anything of the size. Then the war with France comes on, and the bronze reserved for the cast goes to be made into cannon. The clay stands in the open. Six years later French crossbowmen use it as a target and the weather takes the rest.
suggested_refs: Leonardo's notebooks on the gran cavallo and the casting method
sources: Leonardo's notebooks on the gran cavallo

stops.name: Vigevano, the model town and the water
stops.date_confidence: range: the hydraulic folios and the Vigevano work are placed c. 1494-1499 and cannot be fixed to a year
stops.campa: Ludovico's model town gives him water to work with. He sketches locks and sluices for the irrigation of the ducal farm, measures the fall of the ground, and draws the arcaded square going up in front of the castle. The Adda and the Ticino are to be tied into the Milanese canal system so that boats can come down to the city walls. Some of it is built and some of it stays on paper, and it is not possible now to say which folios describe a thing he saw dug and which describe a thing he only wanted.
suggested_refs: The hydraulic folios of the Codex Atlanticus and the Piazza Ducale at Vigevano

stops.name: Milan, Santa Maria delle Grazie: the wall that would not hold
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1495-1498 by documentary and stylistic dating; neither the start nor the completion is fixed to a day
stops.campa: On the end wall of the friars' dining hall he sets the table at the instant after Jesus says that one of the twelve will betray him, and paints the sentence travelling outward through the men in four groups. He wants to work slowly and to go back over passages, so he lays oil and tempera on dry plaster instead of painting into wet lime. The wall begins shedding within twenty years. Matteo Bandello, a friar here as a boy, remembers him standing before it half a day and leaving without touching it. Mark Twain, three and a half centuries on, will call the thing a wreck and the reverence around it a fraud.
suggested_refs: The refectory of Santa Maria delle Grazie and the conservation record of the mural
sources: Santa Maria delle Grazie commission records

stops.name: Milan, Sala delle Asse: the painted bower
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1498 by the castle documentation; the months of work are not recorded
stops.campa: In a corner room of the castle he takes the whole vault and turns it into a bower: sixteen mulberry trees rising out of painted rock, their branches meeting overhead and knotted through with a gold cord that never breaks and never quite resolves. Mulberry is moro. The duke is il Moro. The room is a heraldic joke told at the scale of a ceiling, and it is the last thing Leonardo makes for Ludovico Sforza. It was whitewashed over for centuries and is still being uncovered.
suggested_refs: The Sala delle Asse vault, Castello Sforzesco, and its restoration record

stops.name: Milan, the French come in
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1499 for the fall of Ludovico and Leonardo's departure; the month of his leaving is inferred from his deposit of funds in Florence
stops.campa: Louis XII takes the city and Ludovico is carried off to die in a French cell. Leonardo packs the notebooks, sends six hundred florins to a bank in Florence, and goes. Behind him the clay horse stands in the courtyard and the Gascon archers shoot at it; the Last Supper is already flaking on the refectory wall. Seventeen years of work in one city, and what leaves with him is paper. He is forty-seven, with no patron and no city, and the road east out of Milan goes to Mantua. He leaves in December.
suggested_refs: Contemporary accounts of the French entry into Milan, 1499

stops.name: Mantua, the Palazzo Ducale: a profile in chalk
stops.date_confidence: attested to February 1500 by Isabella d'Este's correspondence; the day is not recorded
stops.campa: Isabella d'Este has been trying to get a painting out of him by letter and gets him in person for a few weeks. He draws her in black chalk and pastel, in profile, the head turned to the left, and pricks the outline for transfer. Then he goes on to Venice, and the portrait she was promised is never begun. She writes to him, to his friends, to anyone who might apply pressure, for the next four years. What she wanted was a painting; what the archive at Mantua holds is her side of four years of asking. The cartoon is in the Louvre.
suggested_refs: The Isabella d'Este cartoon, Musee du Louvre, and the Mantua state archive letters
sources: Isabella d'Este's correspondence, Mantua state archive

stops.name: Venice, the Palazzo Ducale: a plan to drown an army
stops.date_confidence: attested to March 1500 by the Venetian deliberations and Leonardo's own sketches; the day is not recorded
stops.campa: The Turks are on the Isonzo and the republic wants an engineer. Leonardo looks at the ground and proposes not a fortress but a flood: dam the river in the upper valley, hold the water back, and let it go when the cavalry is down in the bed. Movable sluices, a scheme for drowning an army in its own terrain rather than meeting it. The Senate does not build it. The drawings stay in the notebook alongside the studies of currents and eddies he is making at the same time for entirely different reasons.
suggested_refs: Leonardo's Isonzo defence sketches and the Venetian Senate deliberations of 1500

stops.name: Florence, Santissima Annunziata: two days of crowds
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1501 by Fra Pietro da Novellara's letter of April that year to Isabella d'Este; the exhibition days are given by Vasari without a date
stops.campa: The Servite friars house and feed him in expectation of an altarpiece and get, again, a cartoon. Saint Anne, the Virgin in her lap, the Child reaching for a lamb, the whole thing worked in charcoal and white on joined sheets. They put it on show in a room, and for two days Florence files past it, men and women, in Vasari's account as if to a festival. Fra Pietro da Novellara writes to Isabella d'Este that the mathematical studies have made him impatient of the brush. The altarpiece is never delivered.
suggested_refs: Fra Pietro da Novellara's 1501 letter to Isabella d'Este
sources: Fra Pietro da Novellara, letter to Isabella d'Este, 1501

stops.name: Urbino, the citadel of a duke driven out
stops.date_confidence: attested to 30 July 1502 by the dated Urbino notes in Codex L; the research pool's first pass wrongly gave June, the month of Borgia's seizure of the city
stops.campa: Cesare Borgia took the city eight days into the summer by riding through the night and frightening the duke out of it. Leonardo is fifty, and he arrives as architect and engineer to the most feared man in Italy, carrying a passport that orders every castellan in the Romagna to open the gates to him. He spends the end of July drawing the citadel. A dovecote, a staircase, the columns of the palace, a sketch for a lifting device, the profile of the walls and notes on how the stone is laid.
suggested_refs: Codex L, the Romagna notebooks
sources: Leonardo's Romagna notebooks, Codex L and Codex Atlanticus

stops.name: Cesena, the passport of the engineer general
stops.date_confidence: attested to 18 August 1502, the date of Borgia's passport; Leonardo's Cesena notebook entries are dated 6 August 1502
stops.campa: August in the Romagna. He records the way the peasants here carry grapes, two baskets on a shoulder pole, and draws it; he notes the design of the harbour cranes; he complains about the local fashion for cutting windows in a wall without regard for what holds the wall up. On the eighteenth Cesare Borgia issues the passport that names him architect and engineer general and orders the whole territory to assist him. It is the widest authority Leonardo ever holds over other men's work, and it lasts about eight months.
suggested_refs: Cesare Borgia's passport for Leonardo, 18 August 1502, Codex Atlanticus

stops.name: Imola, the town seen from directly above
stops.date_confidence: attested to Leonardo's winter in Borgia's headquarters at Imola, 1502; the month of the survey is inferred from his movements
stops.campa: He walks the town with a compass and a measuring wheel and comes back with a circle: Imola drawn from directly overhead, every street and roofline in true plan, the walls and the Santerno set inside a rose of wind directions, washed in blue and ochre. Nobody has to imagine standing anywhere to read it. It is drafted from measured survey rather than by perspective convention, and among the first maps of its kind in Europe. He makes it at Borgia's headquarters over the winter, for a commander who wants to know how to take a town and how to hold it.
suggested_refs: The ichnographic map of Imola, Royal Collection, Windsor
sources: Map of Imola, Royal Collection, Windsor

stops.name: Florence, back on the guild roll: a silk merchant's wife sits
stops.date_confidence: the guild re-registration is attested to 18 October 1503; the start of the Giocondo portrait is placed around this date on Vasari's testimony alone, there being no contract
stops.campa: He puts his name back on the roll of the painters' guild on the eighteenth of October and takes, among other work, a portrait: the second wife of the silk merchant Francesco del Giocondo, Lisa Gherardini, about twenty-four, in a plain dark dress with no jewellery at all. Vasari says he laboured at it four years and left it unfinished. He does not deliver it to the family. It goes with him to Milan, and to Rome, and over the Alps into France, and it is still in the room with him when he dies.
stops.quote: Leonardo undertook to execute, for Francesco del Giocondo, the portrait of Monna Lisa, his wife; and after toiling over it for four years, he left it unfinished.
stops.quote_source: Giorgio Vasari, Lives of the Most Eminent Painters, Sculptors, and Architects, vol. IV, trans. Gaston du C. de Vere (1912-15)
suggested_refs: The Florentine guild register entry of 18 October 1503
sources: Vasari, Lives, vol. IV (de Vere trans.)

stops.name: Florence, the Salone dei Cinquecento: the Battle of Anghiari
stops.date_confidence: attested to October 1503 for the commission, with work continuing into 1506; the research pool's chronology lens gave 1504 and its geography lens 1503-1506, and the earlier date is the correct one
stops.campa: The Signoria gives him a wall of the new council hall and a subject: the cavalry fight at Anghiari, sixty years back, where Florence beat Milan. He designs four horsemen locked over a standard, mouths open, the horses biting each other. On the wall opposite, Michelangelo is to paint the Florentines surprised bathing in the Arno. Leonardo mixes an oil medium and lights braziers under the plaster to drive it in, and the upper part runs down over the lower. Michelangelo never gets past his cartoon. Neither wall is ever finished.
suggested_refs: Rubens's drawing after the lost central group of the Battle of Anghiari

stops.name: Florence, Piazza della Signoria: where the giant should stand
stops.date_confidence: attested to January 1504 by the committee minutes published by Gaetano Milanesi; the sitting of the twenty-fifth is the one usually cited
stops.campa: Thirty men meet in January to decide where the marble giant should stand: the herald of the Signoria, Botticelli, Filippino Lippi, Giuliano da Sangallo, Leonardo. He argues for the Loggia dei Lanzi, under the arches, out of the weather, set back behind a low wall so that the ceremonies of state are not obstructed. The committee sends it instead to the open door of the palace, in the rain, where everyone will see it. Michelangelo is twenty-eight and Leonardo is fifty-one, and this is the only room the record ever puts the two of them in together.
suggested_refs: The minutes of the January 1504 David committee, published by Gaetano Milanesi
sources: Minutes of the 1504 Florentine committee, ed. Gaetano Milanesi

stops.name: Florence, Palazzo del Podestà: the death of Ser Piero
stops.date_confidence: attested to the hour by Leonardo's own dated note, Richter item 1372
stops.campa: Ser Piero dies at the Palazzo del Podestà, where he has been notary for decades, at eighty, leaving ten sons and two daughters by four wives. Leonardo writes the fact down twice in the same sentence, the hour and then the hour again, as though the pen had slipped its track. He does it in a notebook, between other notes, in the register of a clerk recording a transfer. It is one of only two places in the surviving pages where his father is mentioned at all. The half-brothers will keep him out of the estate, and he will litigate against them for years.
stops.quote: On the 9th of July 1504, Wednesday, at seven o'clock, died Ser Piero da Vinci, notary at the Palazzo del Podesta, my father, at seven o'clock, being eighty years old, leaving behind ten sons and two daughters.
stops.quote_source: Dated note, item 1372, The Notebooks of Leonardo Da Vinci, trans. Jean Paul Richter (1883)
suggested_refs: Richter item 1372 and the editor's note on Leonardo's silence about his father

stops.name: Fiesole, Monte Ceceri: the great bird
stops.date_confidence: the Codex on the Flight of Birds is dated c. 1505 and its lines about the great bird are authentic; the manned test flight from this hill is a modern legend traced to Merezhkovsky's 1900 novel, which sets the crash in Milan, and has no contemporary documentation at all
stops.campa: The hill above Fiesole is called Ceceri, and on the second cover of the little notebook on the flight of birds he writes that the great bird will take its first flight from the back of its great Cecero. Ceceri is the mountain; ceceri is also what Florentines call swans, for the chickpea knob on the beak, and the sentence means both at once. He has by now drawn the bat wing, the screw, the parachute, the man lying prone in a frame of ash and canvas. Whether anything was ever carried up this hill and let go, no document says.
stops.quote: Piglierà il primo volo il grande uccello, sopra del dosso del suo magno Cècero, empiendo l'universo di stupore, empiendo di sua fama tutte le scritture, e groria etterna al nido dove nacque.
stops.quote_source: Codice sul volo degli uccelli, second cover recto, Biblioteca Reale, Turin, c. 1505 (the common English rendering 'its great swan' is a gloss on Cecero, not a translation)
suggested_refs: The Codice sul volo degli uccelli, Biblioteca Reale, Turin, second cover recto and f. 18v
sources: it.wikipedia, 'Monte Ceceri', citing Raccolta Vinciana and leonardodigitale.com

stops.name: Florence, Santa Maria Nuova: the cause of so sweet a death
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1507-1508 by the Windsor anatomical sheets; Leonardo gives no day for the old man's death
stops.campa: The hospital gives him the dead. An old man tells him, sitting up and talking quietly a few hours before the end, that he feels nothing wrong with him but weakness. Leonardo opens him afterwards to find out what so sweet a death was made of, and finds the vessels dried and narrowed and the blood not moving. He draws the coronary arteries and describes what will later be called arteriosclerosis. In the same period he dissects a child of two months and notes that everything in it runs the other way: soft, full, wet.
suggested_refs: The Windsor Anatomical Manuscripts, the old man and the two-month child
sources: Leonardo's anatomical notebooks, Windsor Anatomical Manuscripts

segments.name: The French Governor and the Pope's Garden

stops.name: Milan, painter and engineer in ordinary to the king
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: the title is attested in French royal correspondence of 1507 and the recall by Charles d'Amboise is documented, but the residence runs loosely from 1506 to 1513 and cannot be fixed to a date
stops.campa: The governor Charles d'Amboise wants him back, and the Florentine Signoria, still waiting for its wall, is overruled by the king of France. He returns to Milan as painter and engineer in ordinary to Louis XII, with the vineyard the Sforza had given him restored to him. He paints very little. The pages fill instead with the anatomy of the heart, the geology of the Alpine valleys, the way water moves against a bank. For d'Amboise he plans a garden with a watermill in it that is meant to make music.
suggested_refs: French royal correspondence of 1507 naming Leonardo peintre et ingenieur ordinaire

stops.name: Vaprio d'Adda, the Melzi villa above the river
stops.date_confidence: range, c. 1507-1513, with no year fixed. The coordinates are corrected: the research pool's two lenses gave 45.6167, 9.4667 and 45.6167, 9.5167 for this one village, and both were wrong
stops.campa: The Melzi have a villa on a terrace above the Adda, and he stays there for long stretches with the boy of the house, Francesco, who is fourteen or so when they meet and who will be the one to carry the papers home. From the terrace he watches the river cut its bank, and studies how water strips stone, how a current divides around an obstruction, how sediment settles out of it. He designs a canal to make the upper Adda navigable. The drawings of the ferry and the bend below the house can still be matched to the ground.
suggested_refs: The Adda river studies in the Codex Atlanticus and the Villa Melzi at Vaprio
sources: Leonardo's notebooks, Adda river studies, Codex Atlanticus

stops.name: Milan, the second horse
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1512 by Wikipedia following the Trivulzio correspondence; the research pool's first pass gave 1511, off by a year
stops.campa: Gian Giacomo Trivulzio, the marshal who let the French into Milan, wants a mounted monument over his own tomb, and comes to the one man in Italy who has designed a bronze horse at that scale and failed to cast it. Leonardo works the costings out on a sheet: the horse and rider, the marble base, the harpies, the columns, the metal and the labour, item by item, in the manner of a builder's estimate. Then the Swiss come down, the French are thrown out, and the second horse joins the first as a set of drawings.
suggested_refs: The Trivulzio monument drawings and Leonardo's itemised costing sheet
sources: Surviving preparatory drawings and Trivulzio correspondence

stops.name: Rome, the Belvedere: rooms, a stipend, and no pictures
stops.date_confidence: attested to late 1513 for the arrival, with the Roman residence running to 1516; the day is not recorded
stops.campa: Giovanni de' Medici is pope and his brother Giuliano takes Leonardo into his household and installs him in the Belvedere, up the hill from the papal apartments, with a monthly allowance and two German assistants. Raphael is painting the Stanze; Michelangelo has lately come down off the Sistine scaffold. Leonardo grinds mirrors, studies optics and the flight of a bird against the wind, plans the draining of the Pontine marshes, and dissects until somebody complains to the pope and the hospital is shut to him. He paints, so far as anyone can tell, nothing.
suggested_refs: The Belvedere Courtyard of the Apostolic Palace and Leonardo's Roman notebooks
sources: Papal court records; Vatican Belvedere residency documentation

stops.name: Bologna, the Palazzo Comunale: a king, a pope, and a lion nobody can place
stops.date_confidence: the December 1515 meeting of Francis I and Leo X at Bologna is attested and Leonardo was probably in the papal train; the mechanical lion is not securely placed anywhere, the pool's own lenses giving Bologna 1515 and France 1517 while the mainstream attribution is Lyon, July 1515, with Argentan 1517 as a rival hypothesis
stops.campa: Francis I has beaten the Swiss at Marignano and comes to Bologna in December to settle terms with Leo X, and the papal train comes north to meet him. Leonardo is very probably in it. Somewhere in this stretch of months a mechanical lion of his walks forward before the French king, halts, and opens its chest to show a bed of lilies. Where it happened is not settled: Lyon in July at the king's entry, this meeting in December, or Argentan two years later. No design for it survives in any hand.
suggested_refs: The Bologna interview of Francis I and Leo X, December 1515
The disputed mechanical lion of 1515-1517
sources: 16th-century Italian chronicle accounts of the automaton lion

stops.name: Amboise, Clos Lucé: over the Alps with three panels
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1516 by French court records and by the royal letter of 21 March 1516 arranging the move; the month of arrival is not recorded
stops.campa: He crosses the Alps at sixty-four, on a mule by one account, with Melzi, the servant Battista de Villanis, and a bundle holding the notebooks and three panels: the Giocondo portrait, the Saint John, the Virgin with Saint Anne. Francis I gives him the manor at Clos Lucé, five hundred metres from the château, a pension, and a title that puts painter first and engineer and architect after it. He is not asked to produce anything in particular. The king wants him in the country to talk to.
suggested_refs: The manor of Clos Luce and the French royal pension records
sources: Antonio de Beatis, travel diary of Cardinal Louis of Aragon, 1517

stops.name: Amboise, the château: five hundred metres and a passage
stops.date_confidence: the friendship and the king's frequent visits are attested by de Beatis and by Vasari; the month here is a placeholder. The pin is the corpus canonical value for the Chateau d'Amboise, about 700 m from the more accurate 47.41368, 0.98603, and is kept for continuity
stops.campa: A passage runs underground between the manor and the château. It is there and it can be walked. That the king used it to come and go unseen is a story Amboise tells about itself, and no document stands behind that part; the pension and the title are another matter, and they are on paper. Francis is twenty-two, and he treats the old man as a possession and a teacher at once. He comes down to Clos Lucé to talk, and says afterwards, in Cellini's report of it, that no man had ever come into the world who knew as much.
suggested_refs: The underground passage between Clos Luce and the Chateau d'Amboise
sources: local Amboise tradition for the king's use of the passage

stops.name: Amboise, Clos Lucé: the cardinal's secretary counts the paintings
stops.date_confidence: attested to October 1517 by Antonio de Beatis's travel diary; the day within the month is given variously
stops.campa: Cardinal Louis of Aragon comes through on a tour of the north and his secretary writes the visit up. They are shown the three paintings. Then the secretary records, plainly and without ceremony, that the old man's right hand is paralysed and that nothing more of that sweetness is to be looked for from him, though he can still draw and can still teach a pupil. Leonardo is left-handed; the drawing hand is not the ruined one. It is the only description of him written by a man who stood in the room.
suggested_refs: Antonio de Beatis, travel diary of Cardinal Louis of Aragon, October 1517
sources: Antonio de Beatis, travel diary, October 1517

stops.name: Amboise, Clos Lucé: the will
stops.date_confidence: attested to 23 April 1519, the notarised date
stops.campa: He dictates to the notary Guillaume Boreau on the twenty-third of April. Sixty masses, and poor men with candles. The books, the instruments, the drawings and all the papers to Francesco Melzi, and Melzi named executor. To Battista de Villanis half the garden outside the walls of Milan and the water rights that go with it; to the servant Maturina a good cloak of black cloth. To the half-brothers in Florence, who had fought him through the courts over their father's estate, the money lying on deposit in Santa Maria Nuova.
suggested_refs: Leonardo's will, notarised by Guillaume Boreau, 23 April 1519, Amboise
sources: Leonardo's last will and testament, 23 April 1519

stops.name: Amboise, Clos Lucé: the death, and where the king was
stops.date_confidence: attested to 2 May 1519 by French records. The deathbed scene is not: Vasari wrote thirty years later, never went to France, and interviewed no witness, and a royal ordinance signed by Francis I at Saint-Germain-en-Laye on 3 May 1519 is the standard documentary objection
stops.campa: He dies at Clos Lucé nine days after the will, sixty-seven years old, reportedly of a stroke. Vasari has the king arriving at the bedside and Leonardo expiring in his arms, and puts him at seventy-four while doing it. Ingres paints the scene three centuries later and it becomes the picture everyone carries. On the third of May, the day after the death, Francis I signs a royal ordinance at Saint-Germain-en-Laye, which is a good deal further from Amboise than a night's ride.
stops.quote: his spirit, which was divine, knowing that it could not have any greater honour, expired in the arms of the King, in the seventy-fifth year of his age.
stops.quote_source: Giorgio Vasari, Lives of the Most Eminent Painters, Sculptors, and Architects, vol. IV, trans. Gaston du C. de Vere (1912-15)
suggested_refs: Ingres, The Death of Leonardo da Vinci (1818)
The royal ordinance signed at Saint-Germain-en-Laye, 3 May 1519
sources: Vasari, Lives, vol. IV (de Vere trans.)

stops.name: Amboise, Saint-Florentin: the grave inside the walls
stops.date_confidence: the burial in Saint-Florentin per the will is attested; the funeral day is not fixed by any document read for this file, and 12 August 1519 is carried from the standard biographies
stops.campa: The will asks for burial in the collegiate church of Saint-Florentin inside the château walls, with masses said there and in two other churches of the town, and the funeral is held that summer. The church stands another two hundred and eighty years. After the Revolution it falls in, and between 1802 and 1810 the owner of the ruins has the stones carted off and sold; the graves are turned over and the marker is lost. From that point on, nobody can say where in the ground Leonardo is.
suggested_refs: The vanished collegiate church of Saint-Florentin, Chateau d'Amboise
sources: Church burial record and Leonardo's will
French Ministry of Culture notes on the Chateau d'Amboise

stops.name: Vaprio d'Adda, the papers come home
stops.date_confidence: attested that Melzi inherited and repatriated the manuscripts in 1519; the month of his return over the Alps is not recorded
stops.campa: Melzi brings the chests back over the Alps to the villa above the Adda and keeps them for fifty years, showing them to visitors, letting nothing go. He compiles the notes on painting into a book. When he dies his heirs have no interest in them. The sheets are given away, sold in lots, cut up, carried into Spain, pasted into albums by collectors who reordered them at will and left no note of the order they broke. Roughly seven thousand pages survive out of perhaps thirteen thousand.
suggested_refs: The Melzi family archive and the dispersal of the Leonardo codices
sources: Melzi family archive history as reconstructed by codex scholars

stops.name: Milan, the Ambrosiana: the Codex Atlanticus comes to rest
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1637 for the donation to the Ambrosiana; the day is not recorded
stops.campa: Pompeo Leoni, sculptor to the king of Spain, buys up loose Leonardo sheets late in the sixteenth century and pastes them into a great album with atlas-sized pages, trimming and rearranging as he goes. The volume passes to the Arconati and in 1637 they give it to the Ambrosiana library, a mile from the refectory wall. Twelve hundred sheets: gears, catapults, water studies, shopping lists, and the draft letter to Ludovico Sforza offering nine kinds of weapon and, tenth, painting.
suggested_refs: The Codex Atlanticus, Biblioteca Ambrosiana, Milan
sources: Biblioteca Ambrosiana, institutional history of the Codex Atlanticus

stops.name: Amboise, Chapelle Saint-Hubert: bones under a slab that names him
stops.date_confidence: the reinterment is attested to 1874; the excavation that produced the bones is dated 1863 by two lenses of the research pool while the chateau's own article implies about 1849, and the discrepancy is left open. No forensic test has ever confirmed the identification
stops.campa: Arsène Houssaye, who has the ruins in his keeping, digs at the site of Saint-Florentin in 1863 and turns up a skeleton and fragments of a slab with the letters EO and DUS VINC still legible on them. He declares it Leonardo. The bones go under a stone in the chapel of Saint-Hubert in 1874, with an inscription that names him without qualification, and visitors have been shown it ever since. No test has ever confirmed the identification, and the sources do not even agree on the year of the digging.
stops.quote_source: Tomb slab, Chapelle Saint-Hubert, Chateau d'Amboise, laid 1874
suggested_refs: Arsene Houssaye's account of the 1863 excavation at Amboise
The 1874 tomb slab in the Chapelle Saint-Hubert
sources: Arsene Houssaye, published account of the 1863 excavation
